problem_statement: Implement `fmt_time_tm_iso8601(char out[20], const struct tm *tm, char separator)` and `scn_time_tm_iso8601(struct tm *tm, const char *str, char separator)`. The first writes an ISO 8601 string into @p out as zero-padded YYYY-MM-DD<separator>HH:MM:SS, using the supplied separator between the date and time, and returns the number of characters written; the full length is 19. It should return -EINVAL for year values that cannot be represented in the four-digit year field. The second parses a string of the same form into @p tm, storing the calendar year in tm_year as year - 1900 and the month in tm_mon as month - 1. It returns 19 when a time part is present and 10 when only a date is present, returns -EBADF if a separator is present but is not the supplied one, and returns -EINVAL for malformed digit or separator patterns. It is not required to reject semantically invalid dates such as month 13 or minute 60 when the textual format is valid.
